newsitem.title: ROMANIA: ROMANIA'S OUTGOING PM DEFENDS CABINET RECORD.
newsitem.headline: ROMANIA'S OUTGOING PM DEFENDS CABINET RECORD.

text.p: Romania's outgoing premier Nicolae Vacaroiu on Thursday defended the record of his cabinet over the past four years, marked by slow reforms, and said the programme of the emerging centrist government was "demagogic".

"The data we have don't show we live in hapiness. But they show we moved into the right direction," Vacaroiu told reporters in reference to the activity of his outgoing cabinet during its four years in office.

He cited the stoppage of the country's economic decline in 1993, relaunch of the industrial and farming sectors as well as ensuring energy reserves for the coming winter among the achievements of his government.

The Vacaroiu government, in office since October 1992, has been under constant attack by the centrist coalition voted in power earlier this month for lack of commitment in carrying out efficient reforms, its failure to liquidate company arrears and its lack of social protection for pensioners and unemployed.
During his four years in office Vacaroiu has survived, with the backing of leftist and nationalist parties, five motions of no-confidence introduced by the opposition in parliament.
On Thursday, Vacaroiu rejected the accusations as groundless and said he had been very affected by the oppositions' attacks.
"What hurt me most was that whenever I agreed with the opposition that, let's say, the walls are white they eventually went out of my office and had said the walls were black."
Latest forcasts say this year's inflation would quicken to 38 percent, compared with a planned 20 percent, also readjusted to 30 percent this fall.
Forecasts put the 1996 budget deficit at 4.0 percent of the gross domestic product, this compared with an initial 2.2 percent, as agreed with the IMF, which was eventually adjusted at 3.0 percent.

Analysts said the new government would be challenged with the hardships left unsolved by Vacaroiu's cabinet when trying to implement the Democratic Convention's (CRD) ambitious plans to improve Romanians' living standars by blending tighter financial measures with increased pensions and benefits.

"Their programme and promises are demagogic," Vacaroiu said. "It's easy to say nice things into a microphone. A country cannot be governed with texts from magazines or with charts. Who is going to give them the billions of dollars they need for their programme?"
Vacaroiu also said the CDR lacked "top experts able to deal with real economy and macro-economic issues."
"God help them keep their promises," Vacaroiu said. REUTER
